vectors.description: subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x10: bit 4 set, SUBGROUP_ID_MODE 0b00 so subgroup_id is 0, priority present) with one 4-byte object
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x10) with two consecutive objects
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x14: SUBGROUP_ID_MODE 0b10, so the Subgroup ID field is present; priority present) with zero-length object
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x30: DEFAULT_PRIORITY, subgroup_id 0) with one object

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set) with one object having empty properties. On a subgroup stream the field is present on every Object and an empty one sets Properties Length to 0, which is legal here and a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a datagram
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x18: END_OF_GROUP bit set, subgroup_id 0, priority present) with one 4-byte object
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x12: SUBGROUP_ID_MODE 0b01, so the Subgroup ID is the Object ID of the first Object transmitted in this Subgroup) with one object
subgroup stream with FIRST_OBJECT (0x40) set — Type Flags 0x50, indicating the first object on this stream is the original publisher's first object in the subgroup
subgroup stream with FIRST_OBJECT (0x40) and END_OF_GROUP (0x08) — Type Flags 0x58, a complete subgroup containing the whole group's data on one stream

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with one object, Object ID 1 (Object ID Delta 1), carrying PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2 and PRIOR_OBJECT_ID_GAP=1. Section 10.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1). Section 10.9: "An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID." Both IDs are at least their gap
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x10) with a normal object followed by an end-of-group status object (status=3). Object Status is serialized only when Object Payload Length is 0
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x10) with a single end-of-track status object (status=4)
subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set) with two objects, each carrying an empty properties blob

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with two objects, each carrying PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2. Section 10.8 makes the Track malformed when "A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap.", so both carry the same value

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with one End of Group status object (status 3) carrying PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=1. Section 11.1.2: "If an endpoint receives properties on an Object with status that is not Normal, it MUST close the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION." Section 11.3.1: "Objects with no properties or non-Normal status set Properties Length to 0."
vectors.error_detail: only a Normal (0x0) Object may carry Properties

vectors.description: subgroup stream whose Type Flags value 0x10 is encoded as the 2-byte varint 8010 rather than the one-byte 10. Section 11.3.1 words its third invalidity rule as "Values of 128 or greater (i.e., any value that requires more than a one-byte variable-length integer encoding)". Those two clauses come apart under Section 8.1's allowance for non-minimal encodings: the value here is 16, well below 128, but its encoding is two bytes. This corpus reads the rule as a bound on the value and is permissive on receive, strict on send, so the vector is decode-only. An implementation that reads the parenthetical as normative will reject it

subgroup stream header with Type Flags 0x16, whose SUBGROUP_ID_MODE is the reserved 0b11 — must close the session. Section 11.3.1 lists three invalid conditions and this is the first: "Values with SUBGROUP_ID_MODE set to 0b11. This mode is reserved for future use." Computing all three rules yields 0x10-0x15, 0x18-0x1D, 0x30-0x35, 0x38-0x3D, 0x50-0x55, 0x58-0x5D, 0x70-0x75 and 0x78-0x7D, byte for byte the enumeration draft-19 wrote into the figure. The bytes after the Type Flags are those of the subgroup-single-object vector, which decodes
vectors.error_detail: subgroup Type Flags 0x16 sets SUBGROUP_ID_MODE to the reserved 0b11

vectors.description: subgroup stream header with Type Flags 0x20, whose bit 4 is clear — must close the session. Section 11.3.1: "Values where bit 4 is not set. Bit 4 MUST be 1 for SUBGROUP_HEADER." This is the opposite of the datagram rule, where bit 4 is reserved and MUST be zero; the datagram conditions do not transfer here, and SUBGROUP_HEADER has no "unspecified bit" condition at all because bits 0 to 6 are all specified for it. A value with bit 4 clear also falls outside the 0b0XX1XXXX stream-type pattern of Table 2. The bytes after the Type Flags are those of the subgroup-single-object vector, which decodes
vectors.error_detail: SUBGROUP_HEADER Type Flags must have bit 4 (0x10) set

vectors.description: subgroup stream header whose Type Flags decode to 144, encoded as the minimal two-byte varint 8090. Bit 4 is set and SUBGROUP_ID_MODE is 0b00, so the value passes the first two conditions and fails the third: "Values of 128 or greater". All values draft-22 defines fit in one byte
vectors.error_detail: SUBGROUP_HEADER Type Flags of 128 or greater are invalid

vectors.description: truncated subgroup header (Type Flags 0x10) — missing publisher_priority
vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading publisher_priority

vectors.description: subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with one object carrying an odd-typed property 0x0D (two bytes, cafe) and PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2 (Section 11.1.2). An odd Type is followed by a Length and that many bytes (Section 8.3); the transport assigns 0x0D nothing, so the entry has no name and its value is the bytes. 0x3C is written as the delta 0x2F from 0x0D

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set) with one object carrying an even-typed property 0x10 = 5, a Type the transport assigns nothing. An even Type is followed by a single varint value (Section 8.3). The entry is kept, without a name

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set) with one object carrying the odd Type 0x0D twice, first with the byte aa and then with bb. The second is written as a Type delta of 0. The Key-Value-Pair structure (Section 8.3) permits a repeated Type, so both entries are kept in wire order

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with one object whose only property is Immutable Properties (0x0B, Section 10.7) holding PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2. Its value is a Key-Value-Pair sequence of its own, whose first Type is a delta from 0 rather than from 0x0B. The contents render as a nested list

subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set) whose object declares a 3-byte property block (Section 11.1.2), inside which the odd Type 0x0D claims 5 bytes of value with only 1 left. The stream frames; the property does not parse, so the Track is malformed for an endpoint (Sections 10.7, 12.1)
vectors.error_detail: property 0x0D claims 5 bytes but the property block has 1 left

vectors.description: subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 1, whose object carries PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2. Section 10.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Group ID Gap 2 is larger than Group ID 1

vectors.description: subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, with two objects carrying PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP 2 and 3. Section 10.8: "A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1)
vectors.error_detail: two Objects in Group 5 carry different Prior Group ID Gap values

vectors.description: subgroup stream (Type Flags 0x11: PROPERTIES set), Group 5, whose Object 0 carries PRIOR_OBJECT_ID_GAP=1. Section 10.9: "An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1)
vectors.error_detail: Prior Object ID Gap 1 is larger than Object ID 0
